MultipleChoice.prompt: The trait below fails to compile. The error says the future returned by the default method `get_or` is not `Send`, because `Self` cannot be shared between threads safely. The default body must keep the `+ Send` promise, because callers spawn the future on a multi-threaded runtime. Which replacement for the flawed line fixes the error without weakening that promise?
reasons: This is a common mix-up. `Send` on `Self` means the value can move to another thread, but the future holds `&Self`. A shared reference is `Send` only when the type is `Sync`, so the error remains.
`Clone` lets you duplicate `Self`, but the default body still captures `&Self` and never clones it. Without `Sync`, that reference still can't be `Send`.
`Unpin` is about whether a value may be moved after being pinned. It is unrelated to thread-safety auto traits, so the error stays.
`'static` limits the lifetimes of references that `Self` contains. It says nothing about whether `&Self` may cross threads, so the `Send` error stays.

The default body's future holds `&Self`, and `&Self` is `Send` only if `Self: Sync`. With `Sync` as a supertrait, the default body can meet its promised `+ Send` for every implementor. The `String` it moves in is already `Send`.
